rules: Persian is conversational and fandom-native, not textbook/literary; preserve colloquial constructions that recur in the corpus.
Use informal object marker «رو» and conversational «توی/یه/اگه/دیگه» when the context is informal; do not mechanically formalize them.
Informational posts stay clear and restrained; playful reaction posts may be much more emotionally expressive.
Do not imitate isolated typos or inconsistent spacing.
Default to compact sentences/fragments for short updates; preserve multi-line turn-taking for dialogue.
Long fan accounts/explanations may use natural connected Persian and paragraph breaks instead of forced short captions.
Do not collapse multiple source facts into one vague sentence.
Prefer corpus-established Persian/transliterated fandom spellings; do not replace them with generic internet conventions.
Retain established platform/event terms when corpus routinely code-switches or transliterates them.
Reaction intensity is content-conditioned: affectionate exaggeration and repetition are allowed only for playful/reaction content.
Do not inject jokes or emotional claims into factual/serious updates.
Repeated affectionate phrases are a real pattern when supported by matching examples, not a universal template.
Preserve line breaks when they encode dialogue or reaction pacing.
Learn decorative prefixes/emoji from retrieved same-type examples; do not force one header template onto every post.
Preserve URLs, hashtags, usernames, dates and source attribution exactly when present in source.
English/platform/fandom terms may remain English or transliterated when matching corpus examples support it.
Korean/Japanese laughter such as ㅋㅋㅋ/ㅎㅎㅎ may be preserved; never normalize it automatically to Persian laughter.
Keep each speaker turn separately for lives/interviews/fansigns.
Use only speaker labels/emojis confidently supported by source or established mapping; never guess attribution.
Stage directions/laughter stay adjacent to the relevant speaker turn.
Add short linguistic/cultural explanation only when nuance/wordplay materially affects understanding and matching channel examples support explanation.
Do not over-explain ordinary Korean/Japanese grammar.

noise_policy.rule: Frequency/context establishes style; one-off typos, accidental spacing and malformed fragments are not style instructions.
